declarations.name: Causal.Causality.not_chronalCurveOn_of_forall_not_lt
declarations.notes: (∀ x y, ¬ C.lt W x y) → a < b → ¬ C.ChronalCurveOn W c a b. ChronalCurveOn.lt_of_lt with s = a, s' = b gives c a ≪_W c b. Correct.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.futureOneConnectedOn_of_forall_not_lt
declarations.notes: Exactly the target's first lemma. FutureOneConnectedOn W (Causal/TimelikeHomotopy.lean:149) quantifies over p q γ₀ γ₁ with C.ChronalCurveOn W γ₀ 0 1, γ₀ 0 = p, γ₀ 1 = q (and the same for γ₁). The proof takes the hypothesis h₀ and applies the previous lemma with zero_lt_one. Vacuity applied correctly. The hypothesis is satisfiable (withoutChronology, the four lines), so the lemma is not vacuous itself.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.withoutChronology_futureOneConnectedOn / withoutChronology_futureOneConnected
declarations.notes: withoutChronology (Causal/LemmaKObstruction.lean:157) has lt _ _ _ := False, so `fun _ _ h => h` discharges the hypothesis. At M via ⊤. As the target words them.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.pushUp_of_forall_not_lt
declarations.notes: True for the right reason. PushUp (Causal/Properties.lean:69) asks only inclusions J±_U(I±_U x) ⊆ I±_U x and I±_U(J±_U x) ⊆ I±_U x, and pushUp_iff (:274) puts a ≪ premise in each clause. With ≪ empty every clause is about ∅. The hypothesis is over every open U, which is equivalent to ⊤ only through lt_mono. Not vacuous: the hypothesis is satisfiable, and the axioms are [propext, Quot.sound].

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.not_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere_of_forall_not_lt
declarations.notes: HasChronalNeighbour p (Causal/LocateExtension.lean:138) is I⁺_⊤{p} ≠ ∅ ∨ I⁻_⊤{p} ≠ ∅. With ≪_⊤ empty both are empty, and [Nonempty M] supplies the point. Correct, and the Nonempty is needed.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.not_causallyPlain_of_forall_not_lt
declarations.notes: True for the right reason. CausallyPlain (Causal/Properties.lean:55) at U = ⊤, A = univ: J⁺_⊤(univ) = univ by le_refl, so its interior is univ, while I⁺_⊤(univ) = ∅ and closure ∅ = ∅. It fails on a non-empty space. The hypothesis is only at ⊤. This agrees with the library's lightlikeLine_not_causallyPlain and with the rational and jump lines' ¬ CausallyPlain.

declarations.name: Causal.halfChronoLine_chronalCurveOn_iff / _iff_strictMonoOn
declarations.notes: halfChronoLine.lt U x y = −1 < x ∧ x < y ∧ Icc x y ⊆ U (#print). (→) drops −1 < x locally, and −1 < c a comes from lt_of_lt, which needs a < b. (←) gives c s ≥ c a > −1 by monotonicity. The a < b hypothesis is necessary, since over [a, a] the iff fails. The strictMonoOn form is the evidence's characterisation, word for word.

declarations.name: Causal.halfChronoLine_futureOneConnectedOn
declarations.notes: Not vacuous: the probe proved halfChronoLine.ChronalCurveOn ⊤ id 0 1. The proof is correct. Both curves are timelike-line chronal curves. Causal.timelikeLine_futureOneConnectedOn (TimelikeHomotopy.lean:646) gives the convex combination Γ t s = (1 − t) γ₀ s + t γ₁ s (read at :658). Each slice starts at Γ t 0 = γ₀ 0 = p > −1 (fix_zero), so it is a half-chronological chronal curve. The other fields of ChronalHomotopyOn do not mention the causality.

declarations.name: Causal.halfChronoLine_not_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere
declarations.notes: At −1: −1 ≪ y needs −1 < −1, and y ≪ −1 needs −1 < y < −1. Correct.

The inline refutations are correct, read against symmRationalLine's definition (StrongCausalityLifts.lean:514). ¬ IsCausal: 0 ≤ 1 ≤ 0. ¬ CausallyCompact: J(0, 0) ⊇ ℕ is unbounded. ¬ CausallyOpenFuture: 1 ∈ J⁺_M((0, 1)) through 1/2, while an irrational v > 1 near 1 is related only to itself. ¬ Tarentin: two distinct irrationals in a diamond would both equal p.
